patch.value: Capture prior field values in the transaction record so a failed update can be truly compensated

The atomic import compensates creates by closing them, which is a real inverse: the item did not exist before, so closing it restores the prior state. An update has no inverse without the prior field values, and this extension does not capture them, so the atomic path deliberately skips update compensation. Writing some other value over a failed update would not be a rollback; it would be a second unreviewed mutation on top of a failed one, which on a partially applied import is a worse outcome than a loud identified failure. Making update compensation sound requires capturing the prior field values into the transaction record before each update and compensating from that record. That changes the transaction record format, so it is a real capability with real cost rather than part of a buffer overrun fix. Raised by a Greptile review of PR 59, where the narrower guarantee that no mutation is left un-identified was accepted as the honest ceiling for that PR.

The transaction record stores the prior values of every field an update will modify, written before the update subprocess runs; compensation restores those values rather than writing an invented value; the record format change is versioned so an in-flight transaction written by an older version is detected and refused rather than mis-restored; a regression test drives a mid-import failure after an update and asserts the pre-import field values are restored exactly
